intake: spiritual-unaffiliated: panpsychist-leaning; raised LDS in Utah and left it; I think experience is a basic feature of the world, not something a brain manufactures and not a person who answers prayers.

walk.note: That is exactly how it went for me; the story arrived before the questions did.
Testimony-only is a fair description of the record, and looking in the world rather than the book is the right next step.
I land at doubt with you, but the second horn misreads Aquinas: his God has intellect and will, so 'the personal God classical theism denies' is not what classical theism says.
Against the God who intervenes in heart surgeries, yes; that is the only God this move actually tests.
I grant that mind does not reduce to matter, but 'two kinds of thing' is not the only way to say so; a monism in which experience is basic fits the same premise.

Elisabeth's objection is good against Descartes, and dependence on the brain is real, but dependence of a subject's contents on a brain does not get you to 'mind is something matter does'; the irreducibility that motivated move 5 is left unanswered, not answered.
'Physics describes structure but not what has the structure' is close to my own reason for being where I am; this is the move I would have made at 5.
I arrive at Subject, but 'the brain is the only structure known to create consciousness' quietly reinstates the premise Dream just set aside; the Lichtenberg hedge is the honest part.
Yes, and I would draw the circle wider than brains, but the move carries.
A choice, honestly labeled as one; I would make the same choice.
Caring before you can prove is a good description of what learned ignorance feels like from inside; the entropy sentence I could not quite connect, but it is not load-bearing.
I take hope, as a choice; I notice the paragraph says both 'if and only if Mercy does what it committed to' and 'a choice, not a proof,' and I read the second as what you mean.
Religion₂ was defined as fidelity and hope, not hope toward a maker; a maker is imported here, and your own last sentence concedes that a maker need not be resolved.
One sentence that says it is a bargain, without saying who bargained what for what; I cannot tell what carried you.

'To think is to ignore' is a fact about attention in finite nervous systems; I see no reason to extend it to any possible mind, and you say yourself Aquinas's alternative has not been shown incoherent.
Suffering is bad for the sufferer regardless; agreed.
I arrive at the question of continuity, not at a dualism; your own caveat that the need is not evidence is what lets me take it.
Standing at the edge waiting for data is where I am too, though I suspect the outside will never prove the inside.

first_exit.why: I agree completely that the mind does not seem to reduce to matter, but that premise does not hand you dualism. It is equally consistent with a view where experience is the inside of what physics describes from outside, which is roughly where your own move 8 ends up three moves later.

comment: The route detours through Dualism and Materialism to arrive, at move 8, at the view that was available at move 5: experience is the inside and physics is the outside. Having gotten there, moves 9 and 10 then lean on 'the brain creates consciousness' again, which is the premise Dream was supposed to loosen, so I would ask you to decide which of those you believe. I respect that you flag your own weak points in the text, but at moves 14, 15 and 16 the flags are doing more work than the moves.
